front_question: What are the major nutrient classes required by the human body?
back_answer: Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats, Vitamins, Minerals, Dietary Fiber (Roughage), and Water.

front_question: Explain the ancient Indian dietary maxim 'Hitabhuk, Ritabhuk, Mitabhuk'.
back_answer: It advocates eating wholesome food (Hitabhuk), eating seasonal food (Ritabhuk), and eating in measured moderation (Mitabhuk).

front_question: What are the nutritional differences observed when comparing potato wafers with roasted chana?
back_answer: Potato wafers contain high fat and sodium with low protein/fiber (junk food), while roasted chana supplies rich proteins, complex carbohydrates, dietary fiber, and minerals (wholesome food).

front_question: Name four native Indian millets highlighted as nutrient-dense superfoods.
back_answer: Jowar (Sorghum), Bajra (Pearl Millet), Ragi (Finger Millet), and Sanwa (Barnyard Millet).

front_question: Why is dietary fiber (roughage) essential in our daily diet even though it yields no direct calories?
back_answer: Roughage adds necessary bulk to digested food, promotes smooth intestinal motility, prevents constipation, and supports healthy gut microbiota.
